topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's scope and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal selection, mutation accumulation, and epigenetic alterations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer initiates and progresses through Darwinian clonal succession driven by both genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies, cancer stem cells, and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue hierarchies, stemness, and the specific cell of origin influence tumor initiation and progression in leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Role of the microenvironment, inflammation, and stroma in tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stromal interactions are required to enable malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the modern sequencing, imaging, and computational approaches used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrated multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesizes how mutational burden, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental coevolution interact to drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It formally concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic of cancer therapy.
